From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: legal view on Acme carve-in request

Team —

I reviewed Acme's redline and the defense-control carve-in. Summary of recommended position (high level):

1) Acceptable carve-in scope (narrow): allow customer to assume defense only for third-party IP claims that are tied to (a) Customer-provided training data or (b) deterministic outputs where the content is materially identifiable as produced from Customer prompts/fine-tuning. We should avoid a blanket carve-in for any allegation that merely mentions customer data.

2) Notice & Handoff: require prompt written notice plus a 14-day window from our receipt of a formal notice to either: (i) assume defense (Redwood), or (ii) allow customer to assume defense. During that window we retain control over evidence preservation. If customer is to assume defense we require a documented handoff that includes an evidence manifest and contact for litigation counsel.

3) Evidence custodian & retention: operationally, ops can export logs to a secure transfer format (ndjson/csv) and we can retain a sanitized copy for 12 months by default. Proposal: customer provides a custodian contact (email) to receive exports and agrees to a secure SFTP or Drive link workflow. We should require the customer to acknowledge chain-of-custody steps in the order form (see suggested wording).

4) Billback / remediation costs: allow billback for engineering time if Redwood performs immediate remediation at customer's request, but cap against either (a) a fixed dollar cap per incident ($500,000) OR (b) use an insurance-offset: customer can provide evidence of insurance that covers remediation and defense; if provided, Redwood will coordinate offsets rather than imposing a hard cap.

5) Settlement approvals: Redwood must retain approval rights over settlements that materially admit fault or impose remedies beyond equitable relief; customer control limited to claims where Redwood explicitly declines to defend and in those events settlement authority should be shared with pre-defined notice and indemnity mechanics.

I've inserted redline snippets in ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx — see section 9(b) through 9(d). Operational notes for Jordan/Ben: we'll need a short SOP for evidence pull (who runs the query, export format, retention timeline). Jordan, can you confirm feasibility of 12-month retention and an export cadence? Ben, please estimate typical engineering billback hours for a takedown/remediation project so we can price the $500k cap rationale.

—Kim
Counsel, Redwood Inference
